about.title: Brawley Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Grocery stores, agricultural supply shops, and restaurants along Main Street and the corridors near Rt 111 and Rt 86 see plenty of foot traffic in Brawley, and a wet floor, cracked walkway, or poorly lit stairwell can turn an ordinary errand into a serious injury. California law generally requires the injured person to show the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors in time. That's why what happens in the minutes and days after a fall matters so much. Photos of the hazard, names of witnesses, and store surveillance footage can disappear or get overwritten quickly. We handle premises liability claims and can evaluate what happened to help you understand your options in Imperial County.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. We can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaint records, or inspection history to support that.

items.title: Video and Evidence Fade Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from stores and businesses is often erased on a short cycle, sometimes within days. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can make a real difference in a premises case.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule generally allows recovery reduced by your share of fault rather than blocking it outright.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Brawley?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city or county building, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim process. We can help you figure out which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if the store says I was watching my phone and not looking down?
items.answer: That argument alone doesn't end your case. California's pure comparative fault system generally allows you to recover compensation even if you share some responsibility, with the amount adjusted for your percentage of fault. The property owner still has to answer for whether they knew about the hazard.

items.question: Are there specific areas in Brawley where these falls tend to happen?
items.answer: Businesses along Main Street and near Rt 111 and Rt 86 see heavy customer traffic, which can increase the chance of spills, uneven flooring, or maintenance issues going unaddressed. Every case depends on the specific property and what the owner knew, so it's worth having someone review the details of where and how your fall happened.
